name: bonsai-js
description: A safe, zero-dependency expression language for rules, filters, and templates

paragraphs: A small, safe, typed expression language for rules, filters, formulas, and templates that people other than your developers write. Zero dependencies, runs in any modern JavaScript runtime, and never executes JavaScript.

Who it's for: teams whose customers, admins, or operations staff write logic into the product (eligibility and pricing rules, saved filters, formula fields, notification templates) and who need to reject a broken rule when it is saved, explain its result, and run it safely.
features: Familiar. JavaScript syntax and JavaScript names: a.b, ?., ??, templates, filter, map, includes, toUpperCase. Every function also works as a method, so sum(xs) and xs.sum() are the same call.

Mistakes are caught when a rule is saved, not in production. Declare your data once with t: user.agee >= 18 is rejected with did you mean "age"? and an exact source range, and user.nick.toUpperCase() on an optional…

Every result can be explained. explain() records the value of every sub-expression, and reasons() returns the conditions that decided the result, so a "why was this rejected" screen can list user.age >= 18 and user.plan…

Safe by construction, and every evaluation is bounded. No prototype access, no globals, no calling functions found in data, no conversion hooks, no mutation: user.constructor is rejected when the expression is parsed. A…

One rule, three places to run it. partial() evaluates what it can and returns the rest: knowing only { user: { plan: "pro" } }, user.plan == "pro" && order.total > 100 becomes order.total > 100. bonsai-js/query turns…
